chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, who said:

I asked Al-Reza (peace be upon him), saying, 'May I be sacrificed for you! The people raise their hands during the Takbeer upon the deceased during the first Takbeer only, and do not raise them afterwards. So shall I restrict myself to the first Takbeer as they do, or shall I raise my hands during every Takbeer?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Raise your hand during every Takbeer.'

key_terms.التَّكْبِير: The act of saying 'Allahu Akbar', used here to refer to the specific exclamations in the funeral prayer.
key_terms.التَّكْبِيرَةِ الْأُولَى: The first Takbeer (exclamation) in the sequence of the funeral prayer.
key_terms.الرِّضَا ( عليه السلام ): Imam Al-Reza (peace be upon him), referring to Imam Ali al-Rida (AS).
key_terms.جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ: A phrase of respect meaning 'May I be your ransom/sacrifice for you', commonly used when addressing the Imams.

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on raising hands during the Takbeers of the funeral prayer?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam Al-Reza (AS) clarifies the ritual etiquette of *Salat al-Mayyit* by instructing the inquirer to raise his hands during every Takbeer, rather than limiting the gesture to the first one as was commonly practiced by the general public. This ruling underscores the Shia emphasis on adhering to the specific prophetic traditions transmitted through the Imams, distinguishing their jurisprudence from prevailing customs. The instruction highlights the importance of replicating the exact manner of worship as taught by the Ahl al-Bayt, ensuring the prayer is performed with the prescribed reverence and completeness.
